title: Why prices go up and down
examples: Why are mangoes cheaper in summer?

explain.say: Why does a mango cost more in winter than in summer? Look at the board: a seesaw. On one side, buyers who want mangoes; on the other, mangoes for sale. Right now they balance, and the price stays steady.

draw.text: Why prices go up and down

explain.say: Now look: lots of buyers, few mangoes. Demand means how much people want to buy. When demand is heavier than supply, sellers can ask more, so the price goes up. Have you seen prices jump before a festival?

Now summer comes, and markets from Mumbai to Bangkok fill with mangoes. Supply means how much sellers offer. When supply is heavier, sellers cut prices to sell before the fruit goes bad. Which way did the seesaw tip?

right.label: Mango season
right.ask: Why are things cheaper in season?

explain.say: Here is the clever bit: price pushes things back to balance. A high price makes some buyers stop and tempts more farmers to grow mangoes; a low price does the opposite. Can you guess where the seesaw ends up? Back in the middle!
That balance point is called the market price. Brilliant! Wow: the same seesaw sets the price of tomatoes in Lagos, of World Cup tickets, and even of your favourite trainers.

faq.a: Demand is how much of something people want to buy and can afford at different prices. When more people want it, demand rises.
Supply is how much of something sellers are willing to offer for sale at different prices. A big harvest means a big supply.

faq.q: Why are things cheaper in season?
faq.a: In season, farmers harvest lots at once, so supply is high. Sellers lower prices to sell everything before it spoils.
asks: Why is fruit cheaper in summer?

faq.a: The market price is the price where the amount buyers want equals the amount sellers offer, so the seesaw balances.
In most markets nobody decides alone: buyers and sellers together push the price up or down. Sometimes governments set limits, like maximum prices for bread or fuel.
asks: Does the shop decide the price?

facts: India is the world's largest producer of mangoes.
Prices of seasonal fruit usually fall at the peak of the harvest, when supply is greatest.

quiz.say: Many people want a toy, but the shop has only a few. What usually happens to the price?
quiz.show: Many people want a toy, but the shop has only a few. What usually happens to the price?
quiz.why: High demand and low supply let sellers charge more.

wrong.0: Prices fall when supply is high or demand is low.
wrong.2: A wanted toy would not become free.

quiz.say: In mango season there are lots of mangoes. What happens to the price?
quiz.show: In mango season there are lots of mangoes. What happens to the price?
quiz.why: High supply means sellers lower prices to sell their fruit.

wrong.1: Prices rise when mangoes are scarce, not plentiful.
wrong.2: Plenty of mangoes is good news, not a reason to ban them.
